messages:
maya: Opening PR to add an air-gapped installer preflight and a short how-to for KMS cert rotation in private deployments. Link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/512. Looking for review on examples and wording.
jess: Thanks, sending quick pass. Are we demonstrating operator-driven rotation (bastion) or orchestrated rotation (controller)? Both are useful.
maya: I included both flows — a minimal bastion curl example for operators and a systemd/unit-based orchestrator example for ops automation. See snippets below.
maya: ```bash
# bastion -> internal proxy -> KMS (air-gapped)
export PROXY=http://proxy.internal:3128
curl --proxy "$PROXY" --fail --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/kms-ca.pem \
  -X POST 'http://kms.local:8443/v1/certs/rotate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KMS_ROTATE_TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"force":true}' -sS
# Note: token should be scoped with "kms.rotate" and provisioned from Vault or equivalent.
```
maya: ```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/kms-rotate-run.service
[Unit]
Description=On-demand KMS cert rotation trigger
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/kms-rotate --endpoint http://kms.local:8443 --token-file /etc/kms/rotate-token --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/kms-ca.pem

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
dave: Looks good. Small requests: 1) highlight never using --insecure in docs, 2) add a short section about token rotation and least privilege, 3) clarify that CA rotation is high-risk and should be done with a rollback plan.
maya: Added bullet notes for all 3. Also clarified port (8443) and that internal DNS (kms.local) must resolve from the bastion or network namespace.
oleg: Please add a crosslink to the onprem networking checklist (bastion NAT/DNS/port matrix) and the network port matrix doc. Operators need the exact IP/port expectations.
docs-bot: Placeholder link inserted: docs/onprem/networking-checklist.md#bastion-nat-dns. Replace anchor if the checklist is reorganized.
infra-bot: Heads-up: I added a lightweight CI job (preflight-airgap-rot-9f) that runs the minimal curl against a local test KMS in a container netns. It will fail CI if kms.local doesn't resolve or the proxy is blocked.
jess: Can we add a troubleshooting FAQ for the common failure modes: curl (7) connection refused, TLS handshakes, proxy 407, and token 401? Short actionable steps please.
maya: Done, included steps: check /etc/hosts or internal DNS, test resolution via `getent hosts kms.local`, run `ip netns exec testns curl ...`, verify proxy ACLs and proxy auth, inspect KMS logs for 401/403 and check token scopes.
dave: I made a tiny wording nitfix and added a one-line example for pinning CA with wget for teams that use it.
oleg: If we plan to merge this, ping #eng-runtime so runtime can review CI expectations and the port choice.
maya: Will do. Thanks all, ready for final review then merge.
dave: Approving. Will squash-merge after tests pass. :shipit:
